claims.statement: The Dreamer is a propose-then-dispose runtime per route rather than a blanket no-writes-before-`commit` rule: there is no write tool in the default set (an adaptor's own verbs are *added* to the read-only set, never defaults), an envelope adaptor returns structured data for `accept` to parse, a staged verb adaptor's typed closures validate and stage as the model calls them, while an adaptor whose checked verbs write when called (Lessons) commits inside the sample; in every case `accept` returns opaque `object` payloads that the runtime wraps in `Proposal`s carrying provenance only the runtime knows, `commit` is code that reports what landed and drives the tier's own store, and no tier value type ever appears in `nora/agent/`.

One Dreamer run is a fixed order: read the objective and its digest for this run, re-check the tool subset, render `inputs` before building tools, build tools from names, run `samples` model calls, union and dedupe, cap, screen the raw items, `accept`, stamp provenance, `commit` — each step placed so the next never sees unvalidated model output.

`DreamOutcome.status` is R-27's three-state vocabulary (`ok`, `nothing_found`, `unavailable`) decided at two boundaries: an unreadable sample (prose, truncated or wrong-key envelope, timeout, killed loop) increments `nora_dream_sample_total{status="unavailable"}` and is skipped, and the run returns `unavailable` before the screen, `accept` and `commit` only when no sample was readable (`readable == 0`), so that path reports `written=0` and never reaches `commit`, while a run with at least one readable sample continues and can still finish `unavailable` on an `accept` raise, a `commit` fault or `AccountNotRecordableError`; in every `unavailable` case the watermark is held and no `last_fired_at` slot is stamped, `ok` is computed from what the model returned or from the proposals/rows rather than from rows surviving, and `DreamOutcome.stop_reason` is an optional diagnostic that on its own proves neither envelope readability nor run success nor the absence of writes.

Envelope validation is the runtime's and deliberately small: `parse_envelope` rejects a response over `MAX_ENVELOPE_CHARS` (200 000), tolerates a preamble via `json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode`, takes the last valid envelope rather than the first, and returns `None` for «not read» as distinct from a well-formed empty list for «nothing found».

The per-run item cap is `MAX_ITEMS` (64) unless `AdaptorSchedule.max_items` overrides it; it is applied to the deduped union across samples, is drop-shaped while the watermark still advances, and the drop is counted with `reason="cap"` on the screened counter.

The Dreamer screen runs on the model's raw envelope items after the cap and before `accept` — before any tier type exists — because a parsed object would need each adaptor to expose its own text, an item carries fields the typed parse drops, and item granularity means one poisoned item never costs its siblings the run.

The screen's predicate is `scan_identifiers` plus sink-only patterns (email, 15-or-more-digit id, labelled lat/lng), walking every reachable string including mapping keys; the same predicate is reused for the runtime's screen on adaptor write verbs and as `text_offence`, the Persona store's write screen.

A screen rejection is a `Rejection(index, reason, path)` that never carries the offending text — so a refused phone number is not copied into a log — and every drop increments `nora_dream_screened_total{adaptor, reason}` and logs, raising nothing.

`DreamGuard` is a separate guard rather than a weakened `ReplyGuard` because a Dreamer loop has no terminal verb: it holds no `Deliverer`, has no `terminal` parameter, registers `BeforeToolCallEvent`/`AfterToolCallEvent` only (never `BeforeModelCallEvent`, whose `cancel` ends a tag turn), and structurally cannot end a turn — the stopping condition and wall clock belong to the runtime.

The guard keeps R-7 default-deny and the shared per-tool `CallLedger` ceiling, adds a per-pass memory ration whose (N+1)th call is answered `unavailable` with a reason rather than vetoed, and turns a spent pass budget into a tool result instead of the SDK's raw cancellation error, so an error never invites the retry the ceiling exists to stop.

`DreamGuard`'s after-tool hook clamps tool results — `web_search`/`web_fetch` at 8 000 characters, memory verbs at 4 000 — with a marker naming the cap, because `MAX_ENVELOPE_CHARS` bounds only the outgoing envelope and an unbounded result re-entering the loop could spend the run's whole token context.

`AdaptorBudget` is per adaptor, never one global ceiling, and bounds a sample's turns/tokens/output tokens, a required `timeout_seconds`, the per-pass `max_memory_calls` (default 2), an optional pass-wide `max_tool_calls` and a per-tool `tool_calls` delta; when a deployment sets `[dreamer.budgets.culture]` the Character, Lessons and Persona sessions inherit it, otherwise they fall back to the runtime's `default_budget`.

Two configuration mistakes are boot failures rather than silent no-ops: an adaptor declaring tools outside `read_only_tools()` (or a tool list a grant widens past the ceiling), and a `[dreamer.budgets.<adaptor>.tool_calls]` key naming a tool the adaptor does not declare — which would otherwise run at the table's number while the config file claimed otherwise.

The read-only ceiling is enforced twice with the identical function: `verify_tool_subsets` raises `AdaptorToolError` at startup, and `tool_subset_faults` re-checks inside every run and returns `unavailable` instead of raising, because the corpus hot-reloads and a per-run check drifting from the trusted startup one would be worse than none; the two independent axes are act-vs-read and room-scoped-vs-unit-safe, with `DREAMER_LOOP_TOOLS` refused to any adaptor.

`RegistryToolSource.build` adds its own two guards behind the name-level ones — only a `read_only()` name is ever built, and without a grant the `Room` has no roster source so a slipped-through room-scoped tool answers `unavailable` rather than disclosing — and `AdaptorGrant(home_room=True)` is the one widening, resolved in `home_rooms` for unit-keyed adaptors and `scope_rooms` for scope-keyed ones, falling back to the closed room and counting `nora_dream_home_room_missing_total` rather than guessing a room.

`inputs` and `commit` each run under a wall clock of `store_calls_per_tick × [dreamer] store_timeout_seconds`, where the declared number is a count of awaited collaborator call SITES; its purpose is to turn a store call that never returns into a counted `unavailable` instead of a `(adaptor, key)` that is never ticked again.

The instruction digest is read per run before anything else and covers the doctrine+objective pair, hashed over exactly the joined string that is sent via one `InstructionSet` carrying `text`, `sha256` and `versions`; a digest captured at construction would keep naming the corpus as it was at process start and look correct forever.

The Dreamer corpus is one doctrine file (a second is a startup error), objectives selected by name with required frontmatter (`name`, `kind`, `version`, `applies_to`, `description`, `change_policy`), preludes that replace the shared doctrine for the objectives they name, and skills for the Cognition session — reloaded through `DirectoryWatcher`, with an unknown objective raising rather than assembling the doctrine alone.

`AdaptorSchedule` is a name-keyed mapping value rather than a protocol field (a defaulted non-method member breaks `isinstance` on a `@runtime_checkable` protocol), and its slot is persisted in `dream_schedule_state` — where a missing row means «never fired», not «fired at 0» — after the run and never on `unavailable`, so a 429 cannot burn a whole day's slot and a run that did nothing cannot stamp `last_fired_at`.

The loop resolves one population per `key_kind` — `scopes()` for `scope`, `units()` for `unit`, `adaptor.keys()` for `entity` — and an unknown kind is logged and not run rather than guessed at or silently skipped.

`dream_loop` isolates failure per `(adaptor, key)`, takes its backoff from `supervise_adapter` rather than `prune_loop`, treats a runtime `unavailable` as a failure even though nothing raised (or the exponential could never engage), wraps the whole unit in one wall clock, and counts a unit still in flight as `nora_dream_skipped_total{reason="in_flight_adaptor"}`; watermarks are advanced last and only on `ok`/`nothing_found`.

The live adaptors are `culture` (scope), `character-person`/`character-unit`/`character-nora` (entity), `persona-person` and the three `persona-{room,unit,nora}` collectives (entity), `persona-verdict` (unit) and `lessons` (entity), each gated by its own config section; the four culture-group adaptors are removed by name once a persona index exists or `[culture]` is off, so a cutover never runs two account writers over one entity.

The `note-candidates`, `note-curation`, `note-merge` and `proactive` adaptors were deleted and the generic `DreamSink` port is gone — `propose`/`supersede` survive only in docstrings, `commit` drives each tier's own collaborator, and the single act verb (`remind`) is now a Cognition session closure rather than a registry tool, so no live adaptor declares an act verb.

The Cognition session is Dreamer work but not a `DreamAdaptor`: it has an objective, a prelude replacing the doctrine and a `cognition_grant()`, yet runs through `CognitionAgentRunner` with its verbs held as the session's own closures, and the config refuses a cognition budget that sets `max_memory_calls`, `max_tool_calls` or `tool_calls`.

The contract suite pins the port's behaviour rather than any tier's vocabulary (a legal batch parses, a malformed item is dropped while siblings survive, an empty commit is legal and reaches the sink, `tools` narrows the ceiling, the objective names a file that exists) and runs the runtime's own screen-then-accept-then-commit order; it ships exactly one registered implementation (a fake) with a control that stops the map shrinking, while `tests/architecture/test_dream_store_calls_are_declared.py` derives each adaptor's awaited collaborator sites from its own AST and forbids `accept` from holding any.

`tests/unit/test_dreamer_runtime.py` holds both halves of the per-sample rule against a scripted model: one unreadable sample beside one valid one is `ok` with one row written and one `ok` plus one `unavailable` on `nora_dream_sample_total`, and its all-unreadable control is `unavailable` with zero written, no `commit` call and two `unavailable` samples.

An all-unreadable run's `readable == 0` return happens before the screen, `accept` and `commit`, so the outcome reports `written=0` and no end-of-run `commit` runs — for Lessons that also skips the horizon decay its `commit` applies — but the return is not a rollback of adaptor verbs that already completed inside a sample: Lessons' checked verbs write and commit as the model calls them, so rows can exist while the outcome reports zero, and the per-sample zero-write assertion in the runtime suite belongs to its scripted envelope adaptor's own sink.
